entities.name: Aeacides of Epirus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Aeacides of Epirus was a significant king in Classical Greece who played a key role in shaping the region's politics and culture. As a grandson of King Alcetas I, Aeacides ascended to the throne around 320 BCE and ruled until his death at the Battle of Pydase in 312 BCE. His reign was marked by several notable events, including the Battle of Leucas, where he allied with the Romans against the Achaean League.

Aeacides' legacy can be seen in the continued importance of Epirus as a major power in ancient Greece, and his influence on the region's art, architecture, and literature. His reign also marked the beginning of the end of the Achaean League's dominance in the region.

The impact of Aeacides' reign can still be felt today, with many historians noting that his alliance with the Romans paved the way for future Roman expansion into Greece.

Aeacides of Epirus was a skilled military leader who led his army to several victories against his enemies, including the Achaean League and the Romans. His tactical genius and strategic thinking earned him a reputation as one of the greatest generals in ancient Greek history.

The legacy of Aeacides' military campaigns can be seen in the many cities and towns that he founded or fortified during his reign, including the city of Pydase where he died in battle.
